les: Elektrisiteit uit son, wind en water
kaps_punt: mense is op soek na volhoubare maniere om elektrisiteit te genereer

items.bewering: Steenkool is 'n fossielbrandstof, en jy weet reeds dat dit nie-hernubaar is.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Fossil Fuels' (education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/fossil-fuels): coal is a fossil fuel; 'Fossil fuels are a nonrenewable resource'.

items.bewering: 'n Groot kragstasie brand elke dag duisende ton steenkool.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Medupi Power Station: Exxaro contracted to supply 14.6 Mt of coal per year, about 40 000 t a day. 'Duisende' is a safe lower bound for a large Eskom station.

items.bewering: Die steenkool in die grond kan eendag opraak as ons dit aanhou verbrand.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Fossil Fuels': nonrenewable; new deposits take millions of years to form.

items.bewering: Drie sulke maniere gebruik die son, die wind en vloeiende water.
items.bron: EIA, Energy Explained: Renewable energy sources (eia.gov/energyexplained/renewable-sources/): solar, wind and hydropower are listed as renewable sources.

items.bewering: Die natuur vul hierdie drie weer aan. Daarom sê ons dat hulle hernubaar is. Hulle raak nie op nie, solank ons dit nie vinniger gebruik as wat die natuur dit aanvul nie.
items.bron: EIA, Renewable energy sources: renewable energy comes from sources that are 'naturally replenishing but flow-limited'. The rate condition only really matters for water in a dam. For sunlight and wind it is harmless because it can never be triggered.

items.bewering: Reën vul die riviere en die damme weer met water.
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, hydroelectric power: 'rainfall renews the water in the reservoir'.

items.bewering: Steenkool is anders, want dit het oor miljoene jare in die grond gevorm. Die steenkool wat ons verbrand, word nie gou weer aangevul nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Coal: plant matter decays into peat and is 'converted into coal by the heat and pressure of deep burial over millions of years'.

items.bewering: 'n Speelgoedwindmeul draai wanneer die wind daarteen waai. 'n Windturbine werk op dieselfde manier, maar dit is baie groter.
items.bron: US DOE, 'How a Wind Turbine Works': the rotor turns because the pressure difference across the blades creates lift. A toy pinwheel turns mainly by drag (Wikipedia, Wind turbine, on drag-type designs). The mapping holds at the level the lesson uses it: wind turns the blades. It would only mislead a learner reasoning about blade shape, which the lesson does not do.

items.bewering: Sy lang lemme sit hoog op 'n toring, waar die wind gewoonlik sterker waai.
items.bron: US DOE, 'How a Wind Turbine Works': 'Because wind speed increases with height, taller towers enable turbines to capture more energy'. Wikipedia, Wind turbine: 'The higher the wind turbine will be, the higher the wind speed on average.'

items.bewering: Die wind stoot teen die lemme en laat hulle draai.
items.bron: US DOE, 'How a Wind Turbine Works': the air-pressure difference across the blade makes both lift and drag, and these turn the rotor. Higher pressure on one face is the air pushing on the blade, so 'stoot teen' is a defensible simplification for Grade 6.

items.bewering: Die draaiende lemme draai 'n kragopwekker wat bo-op die toring sit.
items.bron: US DOE, 'How a Wind Turbine Works': 'The nacelle sits atop the tower and contains the gearbox, low- and high-speed shafts, generator, and brake.'

items.bewering: Dit is dieselfde paar as in 'n steenkool-kragstasie: 'n turbine wat 'n kragopwekker draai. Die verskil is dat hier geen vuur, steenkool of stoom nodig is nie.
items.bron: US DOE, 'How a Wind Turbine Works': the rotor turns a shaft connected to the generator, with no fuel involved. A coal station burns coal to raise steam that turns a turbine and generator. The turbine-plus-generator pairing is common to both.

items.bewering: Party kragstasies gebruik water wat van hoog af stroom. Ons noem hulle hidro-elektriese kragstasies. Die water word dikwels agter 'n dam se muur opgegaar. Dit stroom dan deur groot pype af na turbines wat laer af staan.
items.blok: Water wat van hoog af stroom
items.bron: USGS Water Science School, 'Hydroelectric Power: How it Works': 'The dam stores lots of water behind it in the reservoir'; 'Gravity causes it to fall through the penstock'. 'Dikwels' correctly leaves room for run-of-river stations.

items.bewering: Die water stoot hard teen die lemme, en elke turbine draai 'n kragopwekker.
items.blok: Water wat van hoog af stroom
items.bron: USGS, 'Hydroelectric Power: How it Works': the turbine propeller 'is turned by the moving water'; 'The shaft from the turbine goes up into the generator'.

items.bewering: Die water self word nie opgebruik nie. Dit loop onder by die stasie uit en verder met die rivier af. Reën vul die dam later weer aan.
items.blok: Water wat van hoog af stroom
items.bron: USGS, 'Hydroelectric Power: How it Works': 'The water continues past the propellor through the tailrace into the river past the dam'; 'rainfall renews the water in the reservoir'. The dam loses some water to evaporation, but the generating process itself does not use water up.

items.bewering: Die sonpaneel is die een wat heeltemal anders werk. Daar is geen turbine en geen kragopwekker nie. Niks draai en niks brand nie. Sonlig val op die plat paneel, en die paneel self maak elektrisiteit.
items.bron: EIA, 'Photovoltaics and electricity': 'A photovoltaic (PV) cell ... is a nonmechanical device that converts sunlight directly into electricity.' Among the lesson's three methods, it is the only one without a turbine.

items.bewering: Dit maak net elektrisiteit solank die lig daarop val.
items.bron: EIA, 'Photovoltaics and electricity': PV converts sunlight directly into electricity, and batteries are needed 'to provide electricity when the sun is not shining'.

items.bewering: Jy sien sonpanele op dakke en soms in lang rye op oop veld.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Solar power in South Africa: utility-scale PV plants in the Northern Cape (Kalkbult 75 MW; Jasper 96 MW, 'equivalent to 205 football pitches'), plus widespread small-scale rooftop PV.

items.bewering: 'n Sonkragwaterverwarmer op 'n dak kan amper so lyk, maar dit maak water warm en nie elektrisiteit nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Solar water heating: 'heating water by sunlight, using a solar thermal collector'; flat-plate collectors are 'usually mounted on a nearby roof'. This is a different technology from PV.

items.bewering: Die son en die wind kos niks, maar panele en turbines kos baie geld om te bou.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Cost of electricity by source: 'renewable energies need no fuel'; for wind and solar, cost is 'nearly all sunk-cost capital investment'.

items.bewering: 'n Sonpaneel maak snags niks en minder wanneer dit bewolk is.
items.bron: EIA, 'Photovoltaics and electricity': panels produce most when directly facing the sun, and batteries are needed for when the sun is not shining. Less light gives less output.

items.bewering: 'n Windturbine staan stil as die wind nie waai nie.
items.bron: US DOE, 'How a Wind Turbine Works': the controller starts the machine only at about 7-11 mph. The lesson does not claim this is the only time a turbine stops (it also shuts down at 55-65 mph), so the statement is true as written.

items.bewering: 'n Hidro-elektriese kragstasie het genoeg water nodig, en in droë jare is daar minder.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Kariba Dam (citing Bloomberg 2019 and Washington Post 2023): Zambia cut hydropower production because water levels fell, and in 2023 the level reached 1% of capacity with output limited. The Southern African example matches the claim.

items.bewering: volhoubaar: Op 'n manier wat baie lank kan aanhou sonder dat dit opraak.
items.bron: EIA, Renewable energy sources ('virtually inexhaustible'). This is the standard lay sense of sustainable: able to continue over a long time without depleting the resource.

items.bewering: fossielbrandstof: 'n Brandstof wat oor miljoene jare in die Aarde se kors gevorm het uit die reste van lewende dinge wat lank gelede dood is.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Fossil Fuels': 'made from decomposing plants and animals', 'found in Earth's crust', formed over millions of years.

items.bewering: hernubaar: Wat die natuur weer aanvul. Dit raak nie op nie, solank ons dit nie vinniger gebruik as wat die natuur dit aanvul nie.
items.bron: EIA, Renewable energy sources: 'naturally replenishing but flow-limited'. Read alone, the entry stays true for water, wood and biomass as well as sun and wind.

items.bewering: nie-hernubaar: Wat nie vinnig genoeg weer aangevul word nie, sodat dit eendag kan opraak as ons dit aanhou gebruik.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Fossil Fuels': nonrenewable because 'waiting millions of years for new ... deposits to form is not a realistic solution'.

items.bewering: turbine: 'n Masjien met lemme wat draai wanneer stoom, water of wind daarteen stoot.
items.bron: US DOE, 'How a Wind Turbine Works' (bladed rotor turned by wind); USGS, 'Hydroelectric Power: How it Works' (turbine turned by moving water). Steam turbines in thermal stations work the same way. 'Stoot' is a sound Grade 6 simplification (see the wind item).

items.bewering: kragopwekker: 'n Masjien wat elektrisiteit maak wanneer iets hom laat draai.
items.bron: USGS, 'Hydroelectric Power: How it Works': the turbine shaft goes 'into the generator, which produces the power'. The rotating shaft drives magnets past conductors.

items.bewering: windturbine: 'n Turbine hoog op 'n toring wat draai wanneer die wind waai.
items.bron: US DOE, 'How a Wind Turbine Works'; Wikipedia, Wind turbine (average onshore hub height 103 m).

items.bewering: hidro-elektries: Elektrisiteit wat opgewek word deur stromende water wat 'n turbine laat draai.
items.bron: USGS, 'Hydroelectric Power: How it Works'.

items.bewering: sonpaneel: 'n Plat paneel wat elektrisiteit maak solank sonlig daarop val.
items.bron: EIA, 'Photovoltaics and electricity': PV converts sunlight directly into electricity, and flat modules and panels are the normal form. Read alone, the entry does not also fit a solar water heater, because that heats water and makes no electricity.

opsomming: Every claim in the lesson holds up against DOE, EIA, USGS, National Geographic and South African examples (Medupi, Northern Cape solar plants, Kariba), so it is approved. The only simplification is 'the wind pushes against the blades' (real turbines turn mainly by lift), which is still defensible at Grade 6. Web search was used up this session, so all checking was done by fetching reference pages directly.
